title: WebAssembly instructions: encoding, immediates, stack signature, gating feature

rules.name: The text mnemonic, as binaryang prints it. Two opcodes may share one (select, 0x1b / 0x1c); a name may carry its form ('ref.test null'). Structural markers (else, end, catch, catch_all, delegate) are entries too.
rules.encoding: The opcode bytes, hex: the prefix byte and the sub-opcode as an unsigned LEB128 (fd 80 02 is relaxed SIMD 0x100).
rules.prefix: null, or the prefix byte: 0xfb GC, 0xfc misc, 0xfd SIMD, 0xfe threads.
rules.opcode: The single byte, or the sub-opcode after the prefix.
rules.immediates: In binary order. blocktype (s33), labelidx funcidx typeidx tableidx memidx globalidx localidx tagidx dataidx elemidx fieldidx u32 (u32 LEB), laneidx castflags zerobyte (one byte), memarg (align log2 u32 — bit 6 set: a memidx follows — then offset u32 / u64 for memory64), i32 / i64 (signed LEB), f32 / f64 (4 / 8 bytes LE), v128 lane16 (16 bytes), heaptype (s33), vec(labelidx) vec(valtype) vec(catch) (u32 count, then each). Text: a memarg is written offset=N align=N.
rules.align: Memory access width in bytes — the natural alignment (an atomic must use exactly it).
rules.signature: Operand and result types, bottom of stack first, when FIXED; null when it depends on an immediate (call, local.get, struct.get …) or is polymorphic (drop, select, br). addr: the memory index type — i32, or i64 on a memory64 memory.
rules.feature: The D2 feature that gates it; null: core (MVP).
rules.class: Coarse class: control parametric variable table memory reference numeric-const numeric-test numeric-compare numeric-unary numeric-binary numeric-convert numeric-wide simd simd-memory atomic gc.
rules.proof: Checked by binaryang's tests against its own reader, writer and validator: every entry decodes from its encoding and immediates as ONE instruction and re-encodes to the same bytes (count and width of the immediates; the index space a name claims is checked only where a signature is, below); every signature validates as stated (addr as i32, and as i64 on memory64) and is refused with one operand changed; every gated instruction with a signature is refused with its feature off.
